personal.name: Abimanyu Jayaganesh
personal.headline: CS Engineer & Creative Technologist specializing in Physics-Informed ML, Lakehouse Systems, and GPU-Accelerated Pipelines
personal.summary: Computer Science undergraduate with strong research and production experience across Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), vectorized Lakehouse data engineering, GPU-accelerated computer vision, and edge IoT systems.

education.degree: B.Tech. in Computer Science and Engineering

highlights: Designed and evaluated a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) digital twin for EV lithium-ion battery thermal state estimation using PyTorch, MATLAB/Simulink electro-thermal simulations, and ODE-based energy-balance constraints across 522 drive-cycle trajectories (UDDS, US06, WLTP2) and 78M+ time steps.

Reduced unseen WLTP2 autoregressive rollout MAE by 31.2% and maximum temperature excursion error by 65.6% compared to purely data-driven baselines through first-principles physics-loss regularization, input noise injection, and GPU-accelerated mixed-precision training (AMP/TF32).

Engineered a full-stack online learning platform using Spring Boot with dual MySQL and MongoDB persistence, designing scalable REST APIs, asynchronous data synchronization, and automated cascading operations across relational and document stores.

Maintained Grade-A SonarQube quality across 1.6k+ LOC with only 1.8% code duplication by enforcing clean Controller–Service–Repository layered architecture, continuous refactoring, and Agile SDLC sprints.

Built a unified multi-tenant IoT monitoring platform on AWS EC2 using Django and MQTT for real-time distributed telemetry, implementing role-based access control (Admin/Owner/Worker) and reducing cloud infrastructure costs by 1.5×.

Optimized the high-frequency RMS sensor data-processing pipeline to achieve 10× faster real-time visualization performance, delivering technical presentations that secured 3 approved client proof-of-concepts and a cash recognition award.

projects.title: Frame Order Restoration System
projects.subtitle: COMBINATORIAL TSP OPTIMIZATION & DIRECTML VISION PIPELINE
projects.summary: Engineered an automated video reconstruction pipeline capable of recovering the true temporal sequence of randomly shuffled video frames by formulating frame ordering as a Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP) over multi-modal visual descriptors.

visual.alt: Frame Order Restoration Multi-Modal TSP Pipeline Schematic

key_features: Parallel multi-core extraction combining ORB keypoints, HSV color histograms, perceptual hashes (pHash, dHash), edge-density histograms, and color moments
GPU-accelerated pairwise visual distance matrix calculation via PyTorch and DirectML with hierarchical temporal clustering for long sequences
Multi-start Beam Search initialization followed by iterative 2-Opt, sliding-window, adjacent-swap, and segment-reversal local search refinement (>99% frame similarity)

projects.title: Emotional Dependency Detection System
projects.subtitle: PSYCHOLINGUISTIC EMBEDDING REGRESSION IN HUMAN–LLM INTERACTIONS
projects.summary: Developed an NLP framework quantifying continuous emotional attachment and reliance in human–LLM conversations across 4,049 annotated prompts using 768-D contextual embeddings and gradient-boosted regression.
key_features: Framed human–AI emotional dependency as a continuous [0, 1] regression task across 4,049 curated prompts (synthetic, therapist-style, role-play, and human-annotated)
Engineered 768-dimensional semantic representations via Sentence Transformers (all-mpnet-base-v2), outperforming TF-IDF + Linear/XGBoost baselines
Optimized XGBoost regression across 25 randomized-search cross-validation configurations with dataset balancing, achieving R² ≈ 0.81, MAE = 0.10, and RMSE = 0.14

projects.title: Semantic Alignment of Multilingual Embeddings
projects.subtitle: CROSS-LINGUAL GEOMETRY ACROSS 22 INDIC LANGUAGES (IN22 CORPUS)
projects.summary: Conducted a large-scale empirical study of cross-lingual semantic alignment across 22 Indic languages using the IN22 parallel corpus, evaluating transformer embedding geometry across Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Tibeto-Burman, and Austroasiatic families.
key_features: Evaluated LaBSE, XLM-R, and MuRIL across all 22 scheduled Indic languages using intrinsic cosine similarity, graph modularity, and hierarchical family clustering
Demonstrated that explicit translation-pair supervision in LaBSE yields significantly lower language-clustering modularity and stronger cross-lingual mixing than MLM-only pretraining
Performed statistical hypothesis testing and effect-size analysis across Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Tibeto-Burman, and Austroasiatic groups, exposing failure modes of raw cosine similarity

Zero-cloud hardware comparator and interrupt circuits for sub-millisecond safety threshold evaluation and physical actuation
Adaptive sensor-management controller dynamically scaling sampling frequencies, polling schedules, and power states on physiological transitions
